items.title: CYMAT TO WELCOME GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS AND STRATEGIC PARTNERS TO ITS MISSISSAUGA FACTORY ON OCTOBER 28
items.summary: MISSISSAUGA, ON, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cymat Technologies Ltd. m. m. EDST (the "Event"). Following the Event, Cymat expects to issue a public announcement providing further details of the Event. Federal and provincial government officials, representatives of certain of Cymat's existing strategic partners and other invited industry guests are expected to attend. The Event will take place at the factory where Cymat produces its Stabilized Aluminum Foam ("SAF"), and the Company is pleased to welcome its guests to see the production facility first-hand. Event attendance is subject to change. Cymat Technologies Ltd. holds the global rights, through patents and established know-how, to manufacture and sell Stabilized Aluminum Foam ("SAF"), a unique, ultra-light, cellular metallic material. The proprietary production process entails the injection of gases through a molten bath of alloyed aluminum infused with ceramic particles. The result is an advanced, lightweight, recyclable material that exhibits unique characteristics including customizable density and dimensions; mechanical energy absorption; thermal and acoustic insulation; and time, temperature and strain-rate insensitivity. A key benefit of this continuous foam production process is its scalability and resultant low cost of production.

items.title: Bonnie Crombie unveils subway action plan to connect Mississauga directly to Toronto's Network
items.summary: com/ -- Mississauga mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie has unveiled a Subway Action Plan to connect Mississauga directly to Toronto's subway network by extending Line 2 Bloor-Danforth west from Kipling station. The plan sets out the steps she would take in her first 100 days as Mayor, including meetings with government partners, a motion to Mississauga City Council and the launch of a joint business case. Announced on October 20, the proposed extension would run west from Kipling, the line's current western terminus, serve Sherway Gardens and continue into the heart of Mississauga City Centre. Residents would be able to board the subway in Mississauga and travel directly into Toronto's subway network. Mississauga, Canada's seventh most populous municipality with 717,961 residents at the 2021 census, has no subway service today. Toronto's subway already reaches beyond the city's boundaries. Line 1 has served Vaughan Metropolitan Centre in York Region since December 2017, and the province is building a three-station extension of Line 2 east into Scarborough. Crombie's plan aims to give Mississauga a direct subway connection of its own. "I'm running for Mayor because there is important work to be done. I'm asking residents for a mandate to lead Mississauga into its next chapter: to make life more affordable, keep our neighbourhoods safe and build the transportation network our city needs," said Crombie. Within her first 100 days, Crombie would take three steps. First, she would meet with the Government of Ontario, Metrolinx, the City of Toronto and the Toronto Transit Commission to advance a joint business case and seek agreement on its scope, funding, responsibilities and delivery schedule. Second, she would meet with federal representatives to seek support for planning and begin discussions about federal participation in funding the project.

items.title: Freezing property taxes for seniors? Why this would-be Mississauga mayor’s pitch is stirring generational tension
items.summary: Alvin Tedjo’s proposal to freeze Mississauga property taxes for seniors sparks a debate over intergenerational fairness. Dipika Damerla and Alvin Tedjo spar at a mayoral debate at the Mississauga Civic Centre earlier this month. ” A tax break for seniors or fuel for intergenerational warfare? In a municipal election where affordability and rising property taxes are a top concern, a proposal from Mississauga mayoral candidate Alvin Tedjo to permanently “freeze” property tax increases for seniors has opponents claiming working families struggling under hefty mortgages will have to pick up the tab to keep city services running. C. program cited as inspiration by Tedjo has come under fire for benefiting seniors who don’t need the assistance, with reforms becoming a provincial election issue. Tedjo has said that his program would find the right balance to help cash-poor seniors stay in their homes and not burden young property taxpayers, noting that he has a young family himself. One of his mayoral race opponents, Dipika Damerla said Tedjo’s proposal is misleading and could contribute to “intergenerational unfairness” if the program isn’t targeted specifically to low-income seniors. Harry Kitchen, a longtime municipal finance expert at Trent University, was blunt in his assessment.

items.summary: Carolyn Parrish, Bonnie Crombie, Dipika Damerla and Alvin Tedjo have outlined competing plans for affordability, housing, policing and transit as Mississauga voters prepare to choose their next mayor.

items.title: Food Bank Visits Top Half a Million for Second Straight Year Even as Mississauga's Thanksgiving Drive Sets a Fundraising Record
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Food Banks Mississauga's 2026 Thanksgiving campaign raised $857,029, a new record for the drive even though it fell short of its $900,000 goal. According to the outlet, the drive, sponsored by Keurig Dr Pepper Canada, wrapped up Tuesday as the organization marked its 40th anniversary while continuing to face historically high demand across the city. The outlet reports Food Banks Mississauga's network of more than 60 food programs has logged more than half a million visits for a second consecutive year, with the organization estimating someone visits a city food bank every 22 seconds while programs are open. Insauga.com reports the Thanksgiving funds will help keep those programs stocked with fresh and shelf-stable food close to where residents live. According to the outlet, CEO Meghan Nicholls said people turn to food banks for reasons ranging from low wages and high rent to illness, disability or a job that ended, adding that while circumstances vary, the need stays the same. The outlet reports Nicholls credited community donations with letting the organization keep providing relief even as visit numbers remain exceptionally high.

items.title: Cannabis Stop in Mississauga's North End Leads Police to a Loaded Glock and Fentanyl, Police Say
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a traffic stop in Mississauga's north end over an alleged cannabis violation led police to a loaded handgun and a stash of hard drugs. According to police, officers with the force's 11 Division Community Incident Response Team stopped a vehicle near Maritz Drive and Derry Road West, one block west of Hurontario Street, on Oct. 5. Police say the stop began after an alleged Cannabis Control Act violation drew their attention to the vehicle, and officers soon located suspected drugs inside during their investigation. The outlet reports two suspects were arrested and charged following that discovery. According to police, a subsequent search of the car turned up a loaded 9mm Glock handgun fitted with a prohibited 15-round magazine. Police say officers also seized more than 79 grams of suspected drugs, including fentanyl, heroin, crack cocaine and crystal methamphetamine, along with $1,260 in Canadian cash.

items.title: 2,200 Mississauga Aerospace Jobs Hang on Trump's Shifting Stance Toward Bombardier
items.summary: Insauga.com reports U.S. President Donald Trump appears to be stepping back from his threat to block Bombardier aircraft sales in the United States, a shift that could ease concerns for the company's major Mississauga operations. According to the outlet, Trump signalled the change during a rally in Kansas on Monday, saying he would help the Canadian aircraft maker after learning more about its American workforce. Insauga.com reports Trump told the crowd he always viewed Bombardier as a Canadian company and added that the United States would not hurt it given its operations in Kansas, saying he would take care of those jobs. The outlet says the apparent reversal follows a September threat in which Trump declared Bombardier should no longer be allowed to sell its products in the U.S. unless it moved production there. According to insauga.com, that threat had raised concerns about the Quebec-based manufacturer's operations on both sides of the border, including its aircraft assembly centre at Toronto Pearson International Airport in Mississauga. The outlet reports the facility employs more than 2,200 people and sits on a 40-acre campus that includes a 770,000-square-foot final assembly building and a pre-flight hangar, according to the Ontario government.

items.title: Cover your plants: Frost advisory issued in Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: Take preventive measures to protect cold-sensitive plants, trees and crops, Environment Canada says. Environment and Climate Change Canada issues a frost advisory and is warning residents to cover up sensitive plants. It’s been a sunny and warm week across most of southern Ontario, but a chilly evening looms on Tuesday. Environment and Climate Change Canada has issued a yellow level frost advisory for Mississauga and Brampton, warning residents that patchy frost is expected tonight, mainly in areas away from Lake Ontario. The frost advisory extends to St. Catharines, Grimsby and Northern Niagara. According to Environment Canada, frost can potentially cause damage to plants, trees and crops. The cold temperatures impact leaves, flowers and buds still developing on stems. Gardeners can use plastic containers, sheets or bags to cover up their outdoor plants overnight.

items.title: Overnight Low of 1 C Triggers Frost Advisory Across Mississauga, Brampton and Niagara
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Environment Canada has issued a yellow frost advisory for Mississauga, Brampton and the Niagara Region, with chilly conditions expected overnight. According to the outlet, the advisory also covers St. Catharines, Grimsby, Niagara Falls and Welland, where patchy frost is expected mainly in areas away from the lakes. The outlet reports forecasters are calling for an overnight low of 1 C in Mississauga, Brampton, St. Catharines and Niagara Falls, with slightly milder conditions expected closer to the lakeshore. Environment Canada says frost at these temperatures can damage plants, trees and crops still developing leaves, flowers and buds. Insauga.com reports the cold snap is expected to break by Wednesday, with a forecast high of 16 C and sunny skies returning to the region.

items.title: Steel Shiv Fashioned From a Desk Lands Mississauga Man Another 50 Years in U.S. Terror Case
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a Mississauga man already serving time for an ISIS-inspired terror plot has been sentenced to an additional 50 years after stabbing two correctional officers inside his U.S. prison cell. According to the Justice Department, Abdulrahman El Bahnasawy, 28, received the new sentence to run consecutively to his existing 40-year term, bringing his combined sentences to 90 years. The outlet reports the attack happened in December 2020 while El Bahnasawy was serving his original sentence for plotting attacks targeting heavily populated areas of New York City. Prosecutors say he fashioned a weapon from part of a steel desk in his cell, stabbing one officer in the head and face before stabbing a second officer in the hand when she intervened. According to the Justice Department, the first officer ultimately lost his right eye from the injuries, and a pledge of allegiance to ISIS was found taped inside a locker in El Bahnasawy's cell. Insauga.com reports he pleaded guilty in November 2025 to charges including assault with intent to commit murder, possessing contraband in prison and providing material support to a designated foreign terrorist organization.

items.title: Nearly Four Years After Her Death, Hazel McCallion Still Shapes How Some Mississauga Voters Choose a Mayor
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a new survey finds some Mississauga voters are still weighing Hazel McCallion's legacy as they prepare to cast ballots in Monday's mayoral election. According to the outlet, the Liaison Strategies survey conducted earlier this month found McCallion's legacy matters to 75 per cent of residents aged 65 and older when choosing a mayor, compared with 29 per cent of those aged 18 to 34. The outlet reports McCallion built a national and international political reputation during her time as Mississauga mayor from 1978 until 2014, when she was succeeded by Bonnie Crombie, and she died in January 2023 at the age of 101. Insauga.com says that overall, regardless of age, 49 per cent of survey respondents called McCallion's legacy important, while 52 per cent said a candidate claiming to have learned from her makes no difference to their support. According to the outlet, the results are based on a random sample of 1,000 Mississauga residents surveyed Oct. 2 to 4.
